title: Incident triage and escalation process
text:
Incident triage and escalation process

Support records each incident with affected system, observed behavior, impact, time, reproduction steps, and available logs. The on-call analyst assigns a priority based on service impact and checks whether a known runbook already covers the failure. If a command display freezes after reconnect, Support links the incident to the display recovery guide and sends the logs and incident ID to Engineering. Operations may apply an approved recovery step while Engineering investigates the cause. The ticket owner records the decision, status, and handoff, then confirms recovery with the operator before closure. Repeated incidents trigger a knowledge review so the runbook and test procedure reflect what was learned.

title: Release readiness and rollback process
text:
Release readiness and rollback process

Before a software release, Engineering links each change to a defect or approved request. QA confirms the related test procedure has a recorded result and verifies the expected behavior against the release candidate. Operations checks deployment prerequisites, monitoring signals, and rollback instructions. A release owner reviews known limitations and signs off only when unresolved high-impact incidents have a decision. The release notes state the version, affected system, validation evidence, compatibility impact, and rollback path. After deployment, Operations compares monitoring with the expected result and records any incident or correction for the next release.

title: Support to engineering handoff process
text:
Support to engineering handoff process

When first-line Support cannot resolve an incident using an approved technical guide, the analyst prepares a handoff for Engineering. The handoff contains the incident ID, affected system, priority, impact, reproducible steps, logs, attempted actions, and a contact for follow-up. Engineering acknowledges ownership and links the ticket to a test procedure or an existing defect. Support continues communication with the operator and avoids repeating diagnostic work already recorded. Once Engineering identifies the cause and fix, the teams update the incident report and relevant runbook with the validated resolution.

title: Access review and authentication process
text:
Access review and authentication process

Service owners review access to operational systems on a regular schedule. Each account has a named owner, approved role, business purpose, and review date. Support escalates reports of early login session expiration with timestamps and authentication logs, while Engineering verifies session handling with the relevant test procedure. Operations uses approved steps to revoke unnecessary access and records the outcome in the review log. The process prohibits sharing credentials in incident reports or technical guides. A recurring login defect or access exception becomes a tracked improvement with an assigned owner.

title: Knowledge article update and approval process
text:
Knowledge article update and approval process

An incident, test failure, or release change may expose outdated instructions. The document owner compares the current technical guide with validated evidence from Support, QA, Engineering, and Operations. The update states the affected system, new steps, prerequisites, rollback precautions, version, and review date. A specialist checks the revised procedure in a safe test environment before the owner publishes it. The old version stays in history so teams can trace why the instruction changed. Support links future tickets to the approved version and reports unclear steps for the next review.

title: Incident closure and recurrence review process
text:
Incident closure and recurrence review process

Support closes a ticket only after the operator confirms service recovery or the owner documents an approved closure reason. The record includes the diagnosis, action, relevant technical guide, responsible team, and observed outcome. At the weekly review, Operations and Engineering compare recurring failures by system and symptom, including reconnect freezes, duplicate search results, and export errors. QA checks whether a repeatable test exists for each recurring issue. The review assigns actions to improve monitoring, tests, and documentation; it does not treat a temporary restart as a permanent correction.
